docs.title: LOGIQ
docs.text:
Turning scattered logistics data into reliable, proactive decisions.

LOGIQ (Logistics + IQ) is a Business Intelligence decision-support system built for one of Algeria's leading express-delivery operators. It brings data scattered across several operational applications into a single data warehouse. An automated ETL pipeline keeps that warehouse current. On top of it, LOGIQ adds interactive dashboards, proactive alerts and a conversational AI assistant, so that managers decide on evidence rather than intuition.

It covers two business axes — on-demand dedicated transport and parcel delivery — each read through the same three views: Operations, Cost & Profitability and Performance.

The consolidated Overview, the landing page after sign-in (synthetic test data).

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
Business axes 2 — on-demand dedicated transport (Must have) and parcel delivery (Should have) Views per axis 3 — Operations · Cost & Profitability · Performance KPIs 30 — five per view, per axis, each backed by a drill-down data table Source systems integrated 5 operational applications, consumed through 18 REST endpoints Data warehouse 18 staging tables · 55 dimensions · 7 fact tables · 5 aggregate materialised views Schema Fact constellation with snowflaked, conformed dimensions; SCD Type 2 history Data refresh Automatic, daily at 01:00 UTC — incremental, idempotent and observable Test scale ≈ 13.0 M parcels and ≈ 30.5 M parcel-status events (synthetic, production-scale) Warehouse integrity audit 100 % coverage between layers, 0 violations on SCD2 and business-rule checks Access control 5 default roles, view-level RBAC, users provisioned from the company HR system Interface Arabic (right-to-left), French and English · light and dark themes Specification 12 functional and 19 technical specifications (ISO/IEC 25010) Stack Open-source data and application stack (PostgreSQL, Dagster, Django, Celery, Next.js), fully containerised Deployment One Docker Compose stack on a single modest VPS (2 vCPU, 8 GB RAM) Timeline October 2025 – June 2026

About the figures on this site

The production systems could not be connected during the project, so the platform was validated against a faithful simulation of the source systems fed with synthetic, business-realistic data. Every number visible in a screenshot comes from that test dataset, not from real company activity.

docs.title: AI assistant
docs.text:
Every dashboard answers a question the manager already knows to ask: they navigate to the right page and read the figures. LOGIQ adds a complementary way in, a built-in conversational assistant that turns navigate to find into ask to receive.

It lives in a chat drawer available on every dashboard page. A manager asks a question in plain language (French or English) and gets the answer in place: a short sentence with the figures, a chart, or both.

The assistant answering a natural-language question with a chart (synthetic test data).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The assistant is built on a hosted Large Language Model. The model is used strictly to translate a question into a query. It is never the source of the figures.

flowchart TB
    Q["Question<br/>(natural language)"] --> S["1 · Scope<br/>role decides which curated<br/>warehouse views are in reach"]
    S --> P["2 · Plan<br/>LLM writes one read-only SELECT<br/>+ how to present the result"]
    P --> G{"3 · Guard<br/>single read-only SELECT<br/>on allowed views only?"}
    G -- "no" --> X["Rejected"]
    G -- "yes" --> R["Run on the warehouse<br/>under a read-only DB role"]
    R --> A["4 · Answer<br/>themed chart, or a 1–3 sentence<br/>reply from a lighter model"]
  1. Scope — the user's role fixes which dashboards, and therefore which curated warehouse views, are in reach. Only those are shown to the model.
  2. Plan — the model turns the question into a single read-only SELECT over the allowed views, plus a specification of how to present the result.
  3. Guard & run — a deterministic check rejects any query that is not a single read-only SELECT, or that touches a table outside the allowed set. Accepted queries run under a dedicated read-only database role.
  4. Answer — the result is rendered as a themed chart, or narrated into a one- to three-sentence reply by a lighter, cheaper model.
The model proposes; a secure engine checks rights and runs the query read-only.

docs.title: Why it can be trusted
docs.text:
Same access rules as the rest of the platform

The assistant honours the same role-based access control, enforced on the server. A transport-only manager who asks about parcels is politely refused rather than shown data outside their remit.

Auditable answers

Every figure is read from the warehouse, never generated by the model. Each question, generated query and outcome is logged.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: This page moves from what LOGIQ must do (its specifications) to how it is structured: the functional value chain, the global architecture, the technology stack, security and deployment.

docs.title: Actors and roles
docs.text:
LOGIQ is used by the company's own decision-makers, never by the public. Users do not self-register. They are imported from the HR system and activated by an administrator, who assigns each one a role. The role decides which views the user may open.

Default role What they consult General management (Direction Générale) Overview, Parcel Delivery (3 views), Dedicated Transport (3 views) Parcel & cost-control manager Overview, Parcel Delivery (3 views) Routes manager Overview (Route Analysis is future work) Transport manager Overview, Dedicated Transport (3 views) Administrator Every view, plus user activation, role assignment and pipeline history

Permissions are configurable at view level, so the administrator can create new roles as the organisation evolves, without touching the system.

flowchart LR
    BU(["Business user"])
    AD(["Administrator"])
    subgraph LOGIQ
        UC1(["Consult consolidated overview"])
        UC2(["Consult axis dashboards<br/>Operations · Cost & Profitability · Performance"])
        UC3(["Manage & receive alerts"])
        UC4(["Manage own preferences"])
        UC5(["Administer users & roles"])
        UC6(["Supervise the data pipeline"])
    end
    BU --- UC1 & UC2 & UC3 & UC4
    AD --- UC1 & UC2 & UC3 & UC4 & UC5 & UC6

docs.title: Functional specifications
docs.text: Family ID Specification Multi-axis decision consultation FS01 Consult each axis along its three views FS02 Show a consolidated overview of both axes Proactive monitoring FS03 Define threshold rules on sensitive indicators FS04 Alert automatically, through the preferred channel, when a metric drifts Role-appropriate access & personalisation FS05 Show each decision-maker only the sections suited to their role FS06 Save personal filters and view preferences FS07 Customise alert delivery channels FS08 Switch between dark and light themes FS09 Switch the language between Arabic, French and English Administration FS10 Activate HR-imported users FS11 Assign and adjust roles FS12 Supervise the data-refresh pipeline and its run history

docs.title: Functional architecture
docs.text:
Read left to right, LOGIQ is a one-directional value chain. Data leaves the operational systems, is processed and consolidated into one reliable base, and then forks into two decision-ready outputs: presentation (answering questions when they are asked) and alerts (answering them before they are asked).

Functional architecture: from operational sources to decision-ready outputs.

Two further responsibilities cut across the whole chain. Access & personalisation filters every interaction by role and remembers preferences. Administration governs users, roles and the processing pipeline.

docs.title: Technical specifications
docs.text:
The non-functional requirements follow the product-quality characteristics of ISO/IEC 25010.

The 19 technical specifications (TS01–TS19) Characteristic ID Specification Performance efficiency TS01 Analytical views return within seconds, not minutes, over the full national history TS02 Response time stays bounded as data grows, by reading a pre-computed aggregate layer TS03 Analytical workloads are isolated from operational ones Capacity & scalability TS04 Sized for tens of millions of parcel-status events TS05 Refreshed automatically and incrementally, never fully reloaded Reliability TS06 Figures are consistent across every view TS07 The refresh is idempotent and recoverable TS08 Graceful degradation when the analytical store is briefly unavailable Security TS09 Every view gated by RBAC; accounts provisioned from HR, never self-registered TS10 The two financial perimeters are kept strictly separate TS11 Stateless authentication and encrypted transport Usability TS12 Visual-first, readable by non-specialists TS13 Every KPI has a chart plus an on-demand data-table view TS14 Consistent across both axes and their three views Maintainability TS15 Loosely coupled modules on open, non-proprietary foundations TS16 Operational and analytical concerns cleanly separated Compatibility & portability TS17 Source integration depends only on each system's API contract TS18 Accommodates the deferred Route Analysis axis without restructuring TS19 Reproducibly deployable on modest infrastructure

Three characteristics drive the design: performance and capacity (the aggregate layer and the analytical/operational split), reliability (layered, quality-gated, idempotent refresh) and security (RBAC and separate financial perimeters).

docs.title: Global architecture
docs.text:
LOGIQ is built from five blocks: a data warehouse, an automated ETL pipeline, analytical dashboards, dynamic alerting, and role and account management kept in step with the HR system.

Logical viewTechnical view

End-to-end data flow, each block named by its role (source systems shown with generic names).

The same flow with every block mapped to the technology that realises it.

The five source systems expose their data over REST APIs. A Dagster pipeline ingests them and builds the warehouse in four layers. Results land in two PostgreSQL databases (analytical and operational), with Redis as cache and message broker. A Django + DRF backend serves the dashboard, while a Celery worker runs alerting off the request path. The Next.js web client renders everything over HTTPS.

docs.title: Technology stack
docs.text:
The whole platform is built on open-source, free software. Each tool was chosen for stability, performance at national scale, and existing mastery.

Concern Technology Why Languages Python, SQL Mature data ecosystem; set-based transformations in the database Data & warehouse PostgreSQL One robust engine for the warehouse, the operational DB and the test sources Orchestration Dagster Asset-oriented pipeline with built-in lineage and selective re-runs Backend & API Django (≥ 4.2), Django REST Framework API, ORM, authentication and permissions Background jobs Celery, Redis 7 Alert evaluation and notification fan-out off the request path Frontend Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS 3 Type-safe, component-based single-page dashboard Visualisation ECharts, D3.js, Leaflet, Tremor Statistical charts, custom diagrams, maps, KPI cards Infrastructure Docker, Docker Compose, Nginx, Let's Encrypt Reproducible containers, reverse proxy, automatic TLS Test apparatus (not delivered) FastAPI, Faker Simulated source systems and synthetic data

docs.title: Two data planes
docs.text:
The backend connects to two PostgreSQL databases. A database router sends each query to the right one, transparently to the application code.

flowchart LR
    FE["Frontend"] --> BE["Backend<br/>Django + DRF"] --> RT{"Database<br/>router"}
    RT -- "everything else (read/write)" --> OP[("Operational DB<br/>users, roles, alert rules,<br/>preferences, notifications,<br/>ETL run history")]
    RT -- "analytics models (read-only)" --> AN[("Analytical DB<br/>aggregate layer")]

Heavy analytical reads never disturb the running application, and each store can be tuned — and can fail — independently.

docs.title: Security and conformity
docs.text:
LOGIQ handles commercially confidential figures (costs, margins, volumes) and personal data (clients, employees). Security is therefore built into the design from the start, not added at the end.

Access control rests on a governed user base (accounts mirrored from HR, activated by an administrator) and role-based access control at view level:

Role Overview Parcel Transport Admin General management — Parcel & cost-control manager — — Transport manager — — Routes manager — — — Administrator

Sessions use stateless, revocable tokens. Access follows least privilege, and the analytical services are read-only, so no dashboard user can alter the data.

The design is aligned with ISO/IEC 27001, the client's information-security framework, and with Algerian Law 18-07 on personal-data protection:

Obligation How the design responds Need-to-know access RBAC over an HR-governed user base, least-privilege permissions Data minimisation (Law 18-07) Dashboards show aggregated indicators, not individual client records Integrity of source data Read-only layer: LOGIQ never writes back to the operational systems Segregation of perimeters Transport and parcel figures are never mixed Security in transit Everything is encrypted; only the public web entry point is exposed Traceability User activation, role changes and every pipeline run are recorded

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
The whole platform is containerised and brought up with a single Docker Compose command.

flowchart TB
    U(["User browser"]) -- "HTTPS" --> NX["Nginx<br/>reverse proxy + TLS"]
    subgraph VPS["Single VPS"]
        NX
        subgraph NET["Private Docker network"]
            FE["Frontend<br/>Next.js"]
            BE["Backend<br/>Django"]
            OP[("Operational DB")]
            WH[("Warehouse")]
            DG["ETL<br/>Dagster"]
            CW["Worker<br/>Celery + Redis"]
        end
    end
    NX --> FE
    NX --> BE
    BE --> OP
    BE --> WH
    DG --> WH
    CW --> BE
  • Persistence: both databases and the Dagster run history live on named volumes, so redeploying never loses data.
  • Network isolation: a host firewall leaves only the web ports open. Databases, Redis, the orchestrator and the worker sit on a private Docker network.
  • TLS: a multi-domain Let's Encrypt certificate, renewed automatically. Nginx also carries the event stream used for real-time notifications.
  • Hosting: for testing and demonstration, the entire stack runs on one modest VPS (2 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 100 GB disk, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS). The production deployment is to be provisioned by the company.
  • Automation: the ETL runs on schedule, certificates renew themselves, and containers restart automatically on failure or reboot.

docs.title: Case study
docs.text: Logistics operators generate huge volumes of data every day — parcels, trips, expenses, payroll — yet many cannot turn it into decisions. This page sets the scene: who the project was for, how the business works, what was wrong with the existing situation, and what the new system had to achieve.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Algeria's e-commerce sector is growing fast. Registered e-commerce businesses have grown by about 92 % a year since 2020. Market revenue was about USD 1.3 billion in 2024 and is projected to exceed USD 2 billion by 2029. Delivery companies must therefore scale while keeping costs under control.

The problem is rarely a lack of data. It is that the data is fragmented. Operational, HR, expense and transport systems each run on their own data model, so decisions end up delayed, duplicated or simply sub-optimal.

The question behind the project

How can a unified, automated and scalable Business Intelligence architecture turn fragmented logistics data into a reliable foundation for proactive, data-driven decision-making across operations, cost and profitability, and performance?

docs.title: The organisations
docs.text: Organisation Role Profile Ourquilane Host — designed and built the platform Algerian software start-up based in Algiers. It modernises several sectors through digital platforms and decision-support tools, and runs a portfolio of business applications (HR, fleet, expense management, route planning). Yalidine El Djazair Services Client — whose data the platform analyses Leader of express delivery in Algeria: B2B courier services, B2C e-commerce delivery and COD collection, with real-time parcel tracking. Certified ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 27001.

docs.title: The logistics network
docs.text:
Parcels move through a three-tier network. At the top are four national hubs, covering the north, the west, the east and the Great South. Below them sit regional sorting centres. At the bottom, delivery stations handle the last mile.

flowchart TB
    H1["National hub<br/>sorting & transfer"] <--> H2["National hub<br/>sorting & transfer"]
    H1 <--> R1["Regional centre"]
    H1 <--> R2["Regional centre"]
    H2 <--> R3["Regional centre"]
    H2 <--> R4["Regional centre"]
    R1 <--> S1["Delivery stations"]
    R2 <--> S2["Delivery stations"]
    R3 <--> S3["Delivery stations"]
    R4 <--> S4["Delivery stations"]

Arrows are two-way: parcels move down for delivery and back up for transfers and returns. Each delivery station covers a set of communes and assigns parcels to its drivers for the daily tours.

docs.title: Two business services
docs.text:
Parcel express delivery (B2C)On-demand dedicated transport (B2B)

The company's principal activity: last-mile delivery of parcels ordered online, from the merchant to the end customer.

The parcel lifecycle, with the reverse-logistics flow for undeliverable parcels.

Behind these six stages, the operational system records a finer set of statuses. These statuses later drive the Operations indicators.

Phase Statuses (system labels, in French) What it captures Creation En préparation, Prêt à expédier Registered and prepared by the merchant Outbound Expédié Picked up and dispatched into the network Transit Vers Wilaya, Transfert, Reçu à Wilaya Inter-hub and inter-wilaya movement Delivery preparation Centre, Prêt pour livreur, En attente du client At the destination station Delivery attempt Sorti en livraison, En alerte, Tentative échouée Out with the driver, at risk, or failed Delivered Livré Delivered, COD collected where applicable Return Échec livraison, Retourné au centre, Retour vers centre, Retour à retirer, Retourné au vendeur Routed back to the merchant

Each parcel also carries two commercial attributes:

  • Delivery type — Home Delivery (HD) to the customer's address, or Stop Desk (SD) pickup at a station.
  • Price — a delivered parcel and a returned parcel are billed at different rates. A theoretical tariff comes from the zone-based grid, while a real tariff is recomputed from the measured weight and volume. The gap between the two is a direct signal of cost and profitability.

A client company commissions a dedicated vehicle for a specific trip. The process is organised around a single request rather than a parcel.

flowchart LR
    A["Transport request"] --> B["Agreement"] --> C["Pickup"] --> D["Delivery"]

Each request records the vehicle and its crew, the cargo (type, weight, volume, special handling) and the trip's routing and performance (distance, duration, delays, client rating).

The cost of a trip is built up from several components: a fixed base, a distance supplement, pickup, delivery and handling costs, surcharges (night work, perishable goods, insurance), fuel and tolls. Comparing this cost with the amount invoiced is the basis of the profitability analysis.

docs.title: Operational applications
docs.text:
The day-to-day business runs on a suite of in-house applications, each managing one domain. User accounts for all of them are managed centrally through the HR system.

Application (generic name) What it manages Feeds LOGIQ? Core logistics application The overall logistics flow — physical, financial and operational HR system Personnel records, contracts, absences, organisation Expense management system Company-wide expenses, driver payments, reimbursements Payroll system Salaries and payslips Dedicated transport module B2B transport requests and their stops Fleet management application Vehicle maintenance, preventive planning, spare parts — Returns tracking application QR-based tracking and storage of returned parcels — Asset & stock management tool Warehouse stock, IT equipment, phone fleet — Customer-care application Complaint reception, processing and follow-up — Stop-desk queue application Counter queues and temporary parcel storage —

Each application does its own job well. The trouble is that they do not talk to each other, so the same parcel, vehicle or expense ends up recorded in several places.

docs.title: Diagnosis
docs.text:
Seen from a decision-maker's chair, the existing situation shows one recurring pattern: the information exists, but it is dispersed, inconsistent and hard to turn into a clear picture.

# Weakness Consequence 1 Fragmented information No single place to see the company as a whole 2 Duplicated, inconsistent records The same question returns different answers 3 Doubtful reliability of figures Time spent arguing over which number is right 4 Poor availability of information Cross-cutting figures need slow manual reconciliation 5 Manual, time-consuming reporting Spreadsheets rebuilt every time the question changes 6 Reactive management Problems surface only in the next periodic report 7 No consolidated reading per activity Neither axis can be followed along operations, cost and performance 8 Blurred financial perimeters True profitability of each service is hard to establish 9 Limited historical perspective Period comparisons and seasonality are hard to see 10 Dependence on individual knowledge Insight is lost when a key person is unavailable 11 Decisions taken on intuition Partial, late or unreliable information drives choices

docs.title: Gathering the needs
docs.text:
Technique What it brought Individual interviews In-depth view of the returns and operations managers' daily difficulties Group meeting A project-review meeting at headquarters with the department heads Process observation An on-site visit to a sorting centre, following a parcel from pickup to return Document analysis Business processes, parcel statuses, application documentation, earlier theses Application exploration Hands-on use of the operational applications

The needs converged on three families:

  • Informational — one trustworthy source; each activity read along operations, cost and profitability, and performance; separate finances for the two services; enough history to compare periods.
  • Operational — early warning when a key indicator drifts; information matched to each role; decisions grounded in evidence.
  • Quality — reliable and responsive at national scale; simple enough for non-technical managers.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
General objective

Give management a single, reliable and consolidated decision-support system that gathers the scattered data into a faithful, timely view of the business.

  1. Consolidate the scattered data into one coherent, continuously available source.
  2. Read each business axis in depth through three views: Operations, Cost & Profitability, Performance.
  3. Keep the two financial perimeters separate, so each axis is read on its own costs and revenues.
  4. Monitor proactively: signal automatically when a key indicator drifts.
  5. Deliver the right information to the right decision-maker, according to role.
  6. Found decisions on reliable data for both day-to-day and strategic choices.

docs.title: Scope and priorities (MoSCoW)
docs.text:
Priority Scope item What it delivers Must have On-demand dedicated transport (B2B) Full decision support along the three views Should have Parcel express delivery (B2C) The same three-view support for the parcel axis Could have Route analysis Deferred: the data it requires was not available within the project scope Won't have (this time) Other domains (HR, payroll, fleet…) and any operational function LOGIQ is a read-only decision-support layer Why is transport the Must have when parcels are the main activity?

The reason is analytical, not commercial. The parcel axis was already closely watched through real-time tracking. The cost, profitability and performance of dedicated transport, on the other hand, were the most opaque to management and the least served by any existing tool. So that is where consolidated decision support adds the most value first.

Two independent financial perimeters

The costs and revenues of the two services are never mixed. Each axis is read on its own perimeter, so one never inflates or masks the profitability of the other.

docs.title: Methodology and timeline
docs.text:
The work ran in seven phases between October 2025 and June 2026, planned and tracked in Notion.

The seven phases of the project, from literature review to final delivery.

docs.title: Dashboards & alerting
docs.text:
The warehouse holds the data and the pipeline keeps it fresh. The application platform is where decision-makers actually read it: a Next.js single-page application over a role-aware Django REST API, which never touches a database directly.

Synthetic data

All screenshots on this page show the platform populated with the synthetic test dataset.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
The interface follows the way the business reasons: two axes, each read through three views, plus a consolidated overview and supporting areas. Navigation is filtered by role, so the menu itself reflects each user's permissions.

Area What it presents Overview The headline indicators of both axes side by side Parcel Delivery Operations · Cost & Profitability · Performance On-Demand Dedicated Transport The same three views, on a strictly separate financial perimeter Alerts Alerts raised or subscribed to, with status and history Preferences Saved filters, notification channels, theme and language Administration User activation, role assignment, pipeline supervision (administrators only)

Users sign in with the credentials of the company HR system. There are no separate LOGIQ passwords to manage.

The sign-in screen.

docs.title: Visualisation toolkit
docs.text:
The dashboards are visual-first. Each KPI is a chart or graphic, with the exact figures one click away.

Visualisation Library Used for KPI cards Tremor Headline figure, period-over-period delta, severity colour Statistical charts ECharts Trends, comparisons, composition, scatter, heatmap, gauge, radar, Sankey Custom diagrams D3.js Bespoke cost-flow and network visualisations Interactive maps Leaflet Geographic distribution of flows across the wilayas

docs.title: Verifiable KPIs
docs.text:
Every KPI card opens a data-table view that lists the individual records behind the headline figure. Opening Total Requests, for example, shows each request with its identifier, date, service, status, origin, destination, distance and stop count. Every KPI thus becomes an auditable number rather than an opaque one.

The data-table view behind the Total Requests card.

docs.title: Proactive alerting
docs.text:
Presentation answers questions when they are asked. Alerting answers them before they are asked. A user defines a rule on a sensitive indicator: metric · operator · threshold · severity · cooldown.

flowchart TB
    R["Define rule<br/>metric · operator · threshold<br/>severity · cooldown"] --> E["Scheduled evaluation<br/>(Celery worker)"]
    E --> C{"Threshold crossed<br/>and cooldown elapsed?"}
    C -- "no" --> E
    C -- "yes" --> A["Raise alert"]
    P["ETL run events"] --> A
    A --> I["In-app<br/>(real time)"]
    A --> M["E-mail"]
  • A periodic Celery task reads each active rule's value from the aggregate layer. The cooldown stops a still-breached metric from alerting on every cycle.
  • Alerts carry a severity: info, warning or critical.
  • Delivery depends on subscriptions (a user only receives alerts for rules they subscribe to) and on each user's channel preference (in-app, e-mail, or both).
  • In-app notifications are pushed in real time. E-mail covers ETL-run reports, and alerts are grouped into a weekly digest sent every Sunday at 07:00.
Alerts pageDefining a ruleSubscriptionsNotification centreE-mails

docs.title: Preferences and multilingual support
docs.text:
Each user picks a theme (light or dark), their notification channels and the interface language. LOGIQ ships in Arabic, French and English, with a complete right-to-left layout for Arabic. Preferences are stored on the operational database and re-applied at every session.

Preferences (Arabic)Dashboard (Arabic, RTL)

docs.title: Administration
docs.text:
Administrators keep full access to every business page. They also have an Administration area: a platform overview, the Users page (activate HR-imported accounts and assign roles), the Roles page (define what each role may reach), and the ETL Runs history.

The backend also exposes a webhook receiver for the HR system. When an employee is hired, leaves or has their details changed, the matching account is provisioned, revoked or updated automatically.

Admin overviewRoles

docs.title: Graceful degradation
docs.text: The analytical and operational planes are separate, so a brief outage of the warehouse does not break the experience. The analytics endpoints fail safe: they return representative figures instead of an error, and the interface stays usable for real work and for demonstrations alike.

docs.title: Data warehouse
docs.text: The data warehouse is the analytical core of LOGIQ. It is the single consolidated base that every dashboard, alert and AI-assistant answer reads from.

docs.title: Design approach
docs.text:
The warehouse uses dimensional modelling following the Kimball lifecycle. The model is organised around the business questions to answer, not around the source systems. For each business process (parcel delivery, transport request, salary run, expense record), four steps are applied in order:

  1. Select the business process.
  2. Declare the grain — the exact meaning of one fact row, fixed before any column.
  3. Choose the dimensions — the descriptive context: who, what, where, when.
  4. Identify the facts — the numeric measures recorded at that grain.

docs.title: Source scoping
docs.text:
Of the ten operational applications, five feed the warehouse. Each source is sorted into facts (measurable events) and dimensions (descriptive context).

Source (generic name) Data it provides Feeds Core logistics application Geography (wilayas, communes), delivery-centre network, pricing grid, parcel status-event history Geography, pricing and parcel dimensions; the 2 parcel facts HR system Companies, agencies, organisational hierarchy, employees, roles Organisational and HR dimensions (incl. SCD2 agencies and employees) Expense management system Operating expenses, freelance-driver payments, parcel reimbursements Expense dimensions; the charges fact Payroll system Payslips and employment contracts Contract and payslip dimensions; the salary-cost fact Dedicated transport module B2B requests and their stops Transport dimensions; the 3 transport facts

Two points drive the rest of the design. First, the parcel status-event history is by far the largest input, and the only one at a fine, repeated grain (many events per parcel). Second, the HR system is shared by both axes — exactly what conformed dimensions exploit.

docs.title: Four layers
docs.text:
flowchart BT
    STG["<b>Staging</b><br/>faithful, untransformed copy of each source extract<br/>one table per source endpoint"]
    DIM["<b>Dimensions</b><br/>conformed context: who, what, where, when<br/>snowflaked hierarchies, SCD2 where needed"]
    FCT["<b>Facts</b><br/>measurable business events<br/>7 tables, each at a declared grain"]
    AGG["<b>Aggregates</b><br/>pre-computed summaries by period, axis, geography, organisation<br/>what the dashboards read"]
    STG --> DIM --> FCT --> AGG

Each layer refines the one below it. Most importantly, the dashboards read the aggregate layer, not the raw facts. That is what keeps a view responsive at national scale.

Layer Realised in PostgreSQL as Objects Staging One raw landing table per source endpoint, no business logic 18 Dimensions Normalised (snowflaked) tables, SCD Type 2 where attributes change 55 Facts Fact tables keyed to their dimensions, holding the measures 7 Aggregates Materialised views, refreshed each run — the only source of the analytics API 5

The schema is created by ordered, idempotent SQL scripts, one group per layer. The whole warehouse can therefore be rebuilt deterministically from scratch.

docs.title: Schema: a fact constellation
docs.text:
LOGIQ adopts a fact-constellation (galaxy) schema with snowflaked dimensions.

  • Constellation: the seven facts share a common set of conformed dimensions instead of forming isolated stars. Figures therefore reconcile: a cost and a revenue for the same agency and month really do refer to the same agency and month. No fact mixes a parcel measure with a transport measure.
  • Snowflake: every hierarchy is normalised into one table per level, so each attribute lives in exactly one place. A value stored once cannot disagree with itself.
The complete constellation: 7 facts (red) and 55 dimensions, colour-coded by subject area around the conformed dimensions. H = SCD2 (historised), J = junk dimension. Click to enlarge.

docs.title: Modelling techniques
docs.text: Technique Where Why Conformed dimensions Time, geography, organisation, employee — shared by all 7 facts One agreed definition, so figures reconcile across views and axes Snowflaked hierarchies Geographic and organisational chains Each attribute stored once — a single source of truth SCD Type 2 Agencies and employees A fact stays attributed to the agency or employee as it was at event time Junk dimensions Transport cargo and routing flags Many low-cardinality flags collapsed into one row; narrow facts Role-playing dimensions Geography as departure vs arrival; calendar as creation / completion / payment date One physical table reused in several roles Natural vs surrogate keys Natural keys where codes are stable (wilaya, commune, date); surrogates for SCD2 and composite keys Stability where it exists, generated keys only where needed Controlled denormalisation Hire date and company copied onto the employee dimension Avoid nullable or SCD2-unstable join paths Two financial perimeters Express facts vs transport facts Costs and revenues of the two axes never mixed in a fact

docs.title: SCD Type 2 in practice
docs.text:
Agencies get relocated or reclassified, and employees get reassigned. The warehouse must remember what was true when an event happened. A change therefore does not overwrite the row: it closes the old version and opens a new one, each with its own surrogate key and validity window.

flowchart LR
    O["<b>Old version (historical)</b><br/>agence_key = 1042<br/>agency_id = 57<br/>type = Agence<br/>valid_from = 2022-01-01<br/>valid_to = 2024-03-14<br/>is_current = false"]
    N["<b>New version (current)</b><br/>agence_key = 2317<br/>agency_id = 57 (same business key)<br/>type = Hub<br/>valid_from = 2024-03-15<br/>valid_to = NULL<br/>is_current = true"]
    O -- "agency relocated" --> N

A fact references the version that was current at its event date, so history is preserved exactly. All other dimensions are Type 1 (overwrite).

The employee dimension: surrogate key, validity window and is_current flag.

docs.title: Scale
docs.text:
The warehouse is sized for production-scale volumes. The parcel status-event history dominates, at tens of millions of rows. The cost side (payslips, expenses) is smaller, and the transport facts are modest. This scale explains three design choices:

  • the aggregate layer lets a dashboard read a small summary instead of scanning the facts;
  • the refresh is incremental: only new and changed rows are loaded, never a full reload;
  • the analytical store is separate from the operational one, so analytics never disturb the application.

Measured volumes of the test dataset are on Testing & results.

docs.title: ETL pipeline
docs.text: Nothing reaches the warehouse by hand. An Extract-Transform-Load pipeline draws data from each source, reshapes it into the dimensional model and keeps it current, with no manual intervention.

docs.title: An asset-oriented pipeline
docs.text:
The pipeline is not a linear script of imperative steps ("run this, then that"). It is designed around the data assets it produces. Each warehouse table is an asset that declares the assets it derives from: a fact declares its dimensions, an aggregate declares its facts. From these declarations, the orchestrator (Dagster) reconstructs the lineage of the whole warehouse.

What this buys

  • Correct ordering by construction — assets are built in dependency order automatically; nothing is hand-wired.
  • Safe partial re-runs — any single asset, or sub-graph, can be rebuilt without reprocessing everything.
  • Transparency — the dependency graph is itself a readable, auditable map of the warehouse.
The warehouse pipeline as a Dagster asset graph: 18 staging assets, dimensions, 7 facts and 5 aggregates.

docs.title: Five stages
docs.text:
The pipeline advances data through five stages, each mapped onto a warehouse layer. The integration process and the data model therefore share one structure.

flowchart TB
    SRC["Source systems<br/><i>REST APIs</i>"] --> EX["<b>Extract</b>"] --> ST["<b>Stage</b><br/><i>staging layer</i>"] --> LD["<b>Load dimensions</b><br/><i>dimension layer</i>"] --> LF["<b>Load facts</b><br/><i>fact layer</i>"] --> RA["<b>Refresh aggregates</b><br/><i>aggregate layer</i>"]
  1. Extract — pull data from each source through its API, handling pagination and transient failures. Extraction depends only on the published API contract, never on a source's internal database. In total, 18 endpoints are consumed across the five source systems.
  2. Stage — land the raw data, untransformed, in the staging layer. The rest of the pipeline reads staging, not the live sources.
  3. Load dimensions — clean and standardise records, resolve natural keys to surrogate keys, conform the snowflaked dimensions, and version the SCD2 dimensions.
  4. Load facts — resolve each business event against its dimension keys and compute its measures, so every fact lands analysis-ready.
  5. Refresh aggregates — rebuild the materialised views that the dashboards read.
One fact traced back through its staging feed and dimensions, as Dagster records its lineage.

docs.title: Engineering properties
docs.text: Property Why it matters Incremental extraction Only new and changed rows are fetched, from a high-water mark. At tens of millions of events, this is the only tractable option. Small staging tables are simply fully refreshed. Trailing re-window (parcel status) A parcel's status keeps changing after creation, so a pure high-water mark would miss late updates. Each run clears and reloads the last 7 days of status history. Idempotent loads Insert-or-update (upsert) keyed on the business identifier. Re-running a stage never duplicates data. Resilience Failed source calls are retried with exponential backoff. A stalled source is skipped rather than aborting the whole run. Scheduling A full refresh runs automatically every night, plus a lighter dimension refresh. Observability Every run emits lifecycle events (start, success, failure, cancellation). Each run is recorded, and users are notified. Source decoupling Because extraction depends only on the API contract, the same pipeline connects to the real production systems unchanged.

docs.title: Scheduling and observability
docs.text:
Dagster launches a full materialisation every day at 01:00 UTC (02:00 in Algeria), so each morning's dashboards rest on data refreshed overnight.

The pipeline's automation in Dagster: the schedules and the run-status sensors.

When a run finishes, a Dagster sensor calls a webhook on the backend. The backend then:

  1. records the run (outcome, timing, any failure) in the ETL run history;
  2. notifies every user who enabled ETL notifications that fresh data is available, or that a refresh failed.
sequenceDiagram
    participant D as Dagster
    participant B as Backend
    participant DB as Operational DB
    participant U as Users
    D->>D: Scheduled run (01:00 UTC)
    D->>B: Sensor → webhook (success / failure)
    B->>DB: Record run in ETL history
    B->>U: In-app and e-mail notification

This reuses the same notification machinery as the business alerts. A single channel therefore carries both the data's freshness and the business's drift.

The ETL run history, as administrators see it in LOGIQ (test environment).

docs.title: Future work
docs.text: LOGIQ delivers on its four technical pillars: a centralised data warehouse, a reliable automated ETL, interactive dashboards and a proactive alerting mechanism. Both prioritised axes are delivered in full, each on its own financial perimeter. This page sets out the boundaries of that result and where the platform goes next.

docs.title: Contributions
docs.text: Area Contribution Warehouse design Layered dimensional warehouse (staging → dimensions → facts → aggregates) on a constellation schema with conformed, snowflaked dimensions Modelling techniques SCD Type 2 history, junk and role-playing dimensions, controlled and justified denormalisation Data integration Asset-oriented ETL — incremental, idempotent, observable — that depends only on the source contract Operational / analytical split Two stores, so heavy analytics never disturb the application Decision experience Multi-axis dashboards, role-filtered navigation and auditable KPIs traceable to their records Security RBAC over stateless authentication, aligned with the client's ISO 27001 context, on a read-only layer Proactive monitoring Scheduled, threshold-based alerting with in-app and e-mail delivery and per-user preferences Validation apparatus Faithful, production-scale source simulation behind a data-quality gate and a post-load integrity audit

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Simulated, not live, sources. The production systems could not be connected within the project's scope. The simulation's fidelity to the source contract makes it a sound substitute, but the platform has not yet run against the real feeds.
  • No live user-acceptance round. The platform was validated technically, but not yet evaluated formally with decision-makers in day-to-day use.
  • Deliberately bounded scope. Route analysis was kept out of this version because the data it needs was not available within the project's scope.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
Capability Status Condition / next step Route analysis Designed, deferred Awaits routing and optimisation-reference data; the warehouse already accommodates it Live production integration Ready by design Repoint the ETL from the simulation to the real source contracts Formal performance benchmarking Envisaged Measure response times and refresh duration under production load User-acceptance testing Envisaged Evaluate the platform in day-to-day use with the decision-makers Predictive analytics Envisaged Extend the existing facts with forecasts of volumes, costs and performance

Closing word

The project began with fragmented data and a business that could not read its own activity with confidence. It ends with a working, validated decision-support system that consolidates that data, keeps it current, makes it visible along the dimensions that matter, and turns trustworthy figures into the basis for proactive decisions.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: Aggregate layer Pre-computed summaries of the facts by period, axis, geography and organisation. In LOGIQ these are PostgreSQL materialised views, and the only objects the analytics API reads. Asset (orchestration) A data object, such as a warehouse table, that the pipeline produces and that declares which assets it is derived from. The orchestrator builds the lineage graph from these declarations. Business Intelligence (BI) The processes and tools that turn raw operational data into information and insight that support decisions. Conformed dimension A dimension shared, with one agreed definition, by several fact tables, so that figures reconcile across views and business axes. Data warehouse A central, query-optimised repository that consolidates data from several source systems for analysis rather than for day-to-day operations. Decision Support System (DSS) An information system that helps managers make semi-structured or unstructured decisions. Dimension A table holding descriptive context (who, what, where, when) used to filter and group facts. ETL (Extract-Transform-Load) The process that extracts data from sources, transforms it into the target model and loads it into the warehouse. Fact A table of measurable business events (amounts, counts, durations), recorded at a declared grain and linked to its dimensions. Fact constellation (galaxy schema) A dimensional schema in which several fact tables share a common set of conformed dimensions. Financial perimeter The boundary of costs and revenues that belong to one business axis. LOGIQ never mixes the parcel and transport perimeters. Grain The exact meaning of one row in a fact table, for example "one row per transport request". Graceful degradation Behaviour in which a system stays usable, with reduced capability, when a component is unavailable. High-water mark The last loaded position (for instance a timestamp) from which the next incremental extraction resumes. Idempotent load A load that gives the same result however many times it runs, so retries never duplicate data. LOGIQ achieves this with insert-or-update (upsert). Junk dimension A dimension that groups several low-cardinality flags into one table to keep facts narrow. KPI (Key Performance Indicator) A measurable value that shows how well an objective is being met. Materialised view A database view whose result is stored physically and refreshed on demand, making reads fast. MoSCoW A prioritisation method that sorts scope into Must have, Should have, Could have and Won't have (this time). OLAP / OLTP Online Analytical Processing (read-heavy analysis over history) versus Online Transaction Processing (day-to-day reads and writes of the running application). Role-playing dimension One physical dimension used in several roles, such as a date used as creation, completion or payment date. RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) Access control in which permissions are attached to roles, and users receive roles. SCD Type 2 (Slowly Changing Dimension) A historisation technique: a change closes the current row and opens a new version with its own surrogate key and validity window, so facts keep pointing at the version valid at event time. Snowflake schema A dimensional schema in which dimension hierarchies are normalised into one table per level. Staging layer The landing zone that holds a faithful, untransformed copy of each source extract. Surrogate key A generated key with no business meaning, used as the primary key of a dimension.

docs.title: Testing & results
docs.text: A decision-support system is only as valuable as the confidence its users place in it. The production source systems could not be connected during development, so LOGIQ was validated end to end against a faithful test environment. The key property of that environment: the pipeline connects to it exactly as it would to the real systems.

docs.title: Simulated source systems
docs.text:
A dedicated service, built with FastAPI over PostgreSQL, simulates the five source systems behind REST APIs.

Simulated system Domain it provides Core logistics application Geography, delivery centres, pricing grid, full parcel-event history HR system Companies, agencies, employees, organisational hierarchy Expense management system Operating expenses, driver payments, reimbursements, internal transfers Payroll system Monthly payslips Dedicated transport module B2B transport requests and their stops

Why a simulation is enough

Each mock API reproduces the same endpoints, response shapes, authentication, pagination and quirks as its real counterpart. The ETL depends only on that contract, never on a system's internal database. It therefore runs against the simulation without a single change to its extraction code, and the same pipeline would run unaltered against the live systems.

docs.title: Realistic data generation
docs.text:
The data is synthetic but business-realistic, and generated in two tiers:

  1. Real reference data seeds the dimensions: the Algerian administrative geography (wilayas and communes), the network of agencies and delivery centres, the company structure and the pricing grid.
  2. Synthetic transactional data is generated on top: parcels and their lifecycles, payroll, expenses and transport requests.

The synthetic data follows domain rules:

Rule What it reproduces Working calendar The Algerian week — Friday is the only day off; reduced weekend activity Seasonality Ramadan slowdown then pre-Eid peak, Black Friday surge, end-of-year peak Geographic realism Parcel volume spread across wilayas in realistic proportions Labour-law payroll Salaries computed with Algerian labour-law rates Full parcel lifecycle Every parcel goes through its complete multi-status lifecycle Internal consistency Costs, billing and operations reconcile with each other

docs.title: Scale of the test dataset
docs.text:
The dataset is generated at production scale, so performance and correctness are tested under real load. These volumes were read from the warehouse after a full run.

Data domain Volume generated Parcels 13,008,349 parcels (≈ 13 million) Parcel-status events 30,527,458 events (≈ 30.5 million) — the largest feed Payroll 45,378 monthly payslips, for a workforce growing to about 3,000 employees Operating expenses 277,574 expense records, plus 43,668 driver payments and 15,949 reimbursements Dedicated transport 3,822 B2B requests, with 13,414 stops Reference dimensions 58 wilayas, 1,541 communes, 331 agencies, 252 delivery centres

At this scale, the aggregate layer and the incremental load are genuinely put under pressure. On a toy dataset, neither could be meaningfully exercised.

docs.title: Data-quality gate
docs.text:
An automated validation suite runs after every generation. The dataset is admitted to the ETL only when every critical check passes, so any anomaly seen downstream can be blamed on the platform, not on its input.

Check category What it verifies Referential integrity Every cross-system reference points to an entity that exists Financial identities Costs, billing and reimbursements reconcile Distance identities Transport distances are coherent (leg distances sum to the total) Working calendar No operational event falls on a Friday Identifier formats Identifiers follow their expected conventions Test-entity isolation Excluded test entities never leak into the data

The suite has two tiers. Critical checks block the dataset outright. Statistical checks confirm that distributions are plausible (volumes by wilaya, salary ranges, lifecycle proportions).

docs.title: End-to-end validation
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    A["Simulated<br/>sources"] --> B["ETL<br/>pipeline"] --> C["Warehouse"] --> D["Backend<br/>API"] --> E["Dashboards"] --> F["Alerts"]

The whole chain was run as one, and each stage's output was checked:

  • the ETL extracts from the mock APIs and populates every warehouse layer;
  • the aggregate layer feeds the backend's analytics endpoints;
  • the dashboards render the resulting KPIs;
  • the alerting service raises and delivers notifications when a metric crosses a threshold.

Graceful degradation was verified separately. With the warehouse deliberately made unavailable, the analytics endpoints failed safe and the dashboard fell back to representative figures instead of breaking.

A populated Transport Operations page with proactive alerts and the pipeline's run notification in the notification panel.

docs.title: Warehouse integrity audit
docs.text:
After every full run, an automated audit checks that the ETL itself preserved the data through every layer.

Audit dimension What it verifies Result Layer population Every staging table and principal dimension and fact holds the expected rows All populated SCD Type 2 integrity No duplicate current rows, no overlapping validity windows 4 checks, 0 violations Staging → dimension coverage Every source entity reaches its dimension 8 checks, 100 % Dimension → fact coverage Every dimension key is exercised by its facts 7 checks, 100 % Business rules Financial, format and test-isolation invariants hold after load 12 checks, 0 violations

Where a fact holds fewer rows than its dimension, a business rule explains it. Only parcels that reach a billable state produce revenue rows, for example, while every parcel is measured for performance.

Staging → dimensionDimension → factSCD2 integrity Check (source entity → dimension) In staging In dimension Coverage Parcel status history (trackings) → dim_parcel 13,008,349 13,008,349 100 % HR agencies (non-test) → dim_agence (current) 331 331 100 % HR users (non-test) → dim_employee (current) 3,000 3,000 100 % Payslips (non-test, in range) → dim_bulletin 45,378 45,378 100 % Expenses → dim_depense 277,574 277,574 100 % Transport requests → dim_transport 3,822 3,822 100 % Delivery centres → dim_center 252 252 100 % Wilayas → dim_wilaya 58 58 100 %

Verdict

The data served by the simulated sources arrives in the warehouse complete (100 % coverage), correct (zero rule violations) and consistently historised (SCD2 intact). Because the pipeline connects to the simulation exactly as it would to production, this is evidence about the production design itself.

docs.title: Results against the objectives
docs.text:
Objective Result delivered Consolidate the scattered data One dimensional base; figures consistent across every view Read each business axis in depth Both axes navigable through three views, with KPI cards, charts, maps and shared filters Keep the financial perimeters separate Each axis carries its own cost and revenue perimeter Monitor proactively Threshold rules evaluated on schedule raise multi-channel alerts Deliver to the right decision-maker Role-based access gives each manager the right view, plus a consolidated overview Found decisions on reliable data Automatic, incremental, idempotent and observable refresh

On performance, the design choices held up under realistic load. Because the analytics endpoints read the pre-computed aggregate layer rather than scanning the fact tables, the dashboards return within seconds even over the production-scale dataset.

Stated limits

Formal benchmark figures (dashboard response times, refresh duration) have not been measured yet, and no live user-acceptance round has taken place. See Future work.
